points.description: States that the independence assumption does not hold for real internet traffic (answer is "No"), noting that traffic is bursty.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says "no" without mentioning burstiness or dependence, or mentions bursts but the conclusion is unclear.

points.description: Explains why: arrivals depend on previous arrivals (the probability of an arrival is influenced by earlier arrivals), supported by an example such as on-demand video streaming loading segments, giving low utilization right after a segment is loaded.
points.partial_credit: Half if dependence on earlier arrivals is stated vaguely or the example is given without linking it to dependence between intervals.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says independence does not hold, mentions bursty traffic, and explains that arrivals depend on previous arrivals, ideally with an example like video segment loading. Part marks: a bare \"no\" or a vague reason (e.g. \"traffic is bursty\" with no link to dependence). No marks for answering \"yes\" or for reasons unrelated to dependence between arrivals.
